questions.question: How do you define a class and instantiate it?
What does the constructor do and can it be omitted?
questions.answer:
The constructor initializes instance fields and runs automatically when new is called. If omitted, an empty constructor is added by default.

code:
class Greeter {}
console.log(new Greeter());  // works, no error

real example:
Stateless helper classes with no constructor still instantiate cleanly and share their methods.

questions.question: What is the this keyword inside class methods?
What is inheritance and how do you extend a class?
What does the super keyword do in a subclass?
What are static methods and properties?
What are getters and setters in a class?
How does instanceof work?
questions.answer:
instanceof checks whether an object's prototype chain includes a given constructor, which verifies a value was created by a class or its ancestors.

code:
class User {}
console.log(new User() instanceof User);  // true
console.log([] instanceof Object);        // true

real example:
Assertions like expect(body).toBeInstanceOf(Array) guard that an API returned the expected collection shape.

questions.question: What is prototypal inheritance?
questions.answer:
Prototypal inheritance means objects inherit from other objects through a hidden [[Prototype]] chain, and classes are syntax sugar over this mechanism.

code:
const base = { greet() { return 'hi'; } };
const child = Object.create(base);
console.log(child.greet());  // hi

real example:
Understanding that locators and browsers resolve shared methods up the prototype chain explains why them.locator works everywhere.

questions.question: How do you access an object's prototype and create one?
questions.answer:
Object.getPrototypeOf reads the prototype, and Object.create establishes a custom prototype for a new object.

code:
const parent = { x: 1 };
const child = Object.create(parent);
console.log(Object.getPrototypeOf(child) === parent);  // true

real example:
Framework internals use Object.create for lightweight suffix objects, but test code normally sticks to classes.
